meta.source: Port of the Onyx 'Brain' self-improving memory-graph feature (backend/onyx/db/brain.py + brain/tasks.py) into a Rust workspace crate.

product_overview: xai-grok-brain is a Rust library crate in the grok-build workspace providing a durable, single-user 'Brain': a SQLite-backed graph of memory pages with four categories (notes, concepts, entities, workstreams), undirected page-to-page relations, typed source citations, per-store brain settings, and a self-improvement run engine behind a pluggable extraction provider. It ports the Onyx/Perplexity Brain domain layer with parity semantics; HTTP endpoints, UI, and scheduling are out of scope.
core_goals: Durable page store: CRUD with derived titles, persistence across store close/reopen.
Graph parity: undirected relations deduped via ordered pairs, self-edges rejected, related pages grouped by category, graph query with per-node degree including degree-0 nodes.
Provenance parity: typed source citations (chat_session, document, connector, file, manual) with drift-tolerant source-ref normalization ([s1]/S1/[D3]/d4).
Settings parity: enabled/use-connectors flags, clearable focus instructions, last-run timestamp with run-completion stamping.

Engine parity: self-improvement run gated on the enabled flag, transcript built with [S#]/[D#] refs (documents only when use_connectors), focus instructions passed to the provider, pages auto-categorized with update-over-duplicate title matching, sources attached via normalized refs, related pages linked, last_run_at stamped.

key_features.name: Memory page store
key_features.description: Create, read, list (newest-updated first), update, and delete memory pages with title derivation from the first sentence when absent; data persists across closing and reopening the store file.

key_features.name: Relations and memory graph
key_features.description: Undirected page-to-page edges stored once per ordered pair (dedup in either direction), self-edge and unknown-page rejection, edge removal, related-pages query grouped by category, and a graph query returning all nodes with degrees (degree-0 nodes included) plus edges.

key_features.name: Source citations
key_features.description: Typed citations (chat_session, document, connector, file, manual) attach to and list for a page with label capping, and source-ref normalization tolerates bracket/case drift without silently dropping citations.

key_features.name: Brain settings
key_features.description: Enabled flag, use-connectors flag, optional focus-instructions text (whitespace clears), and last-run timestamp round-trip through get/update; a run-completion operation stamps the timestamp; settings persist across reopen.

key_features.name: Self-improvement run engine
key_features.description: run_self_improvement builds an [S#]/[D#]-tagged transcript from session/document context (documents only when use_connectors), passes focus instructions and existing titles to a pluggable ExtractionProvider, applies extracted pages into the four categories with update-over-duplicate title matching, attaches per-page sources via normalized refs, links related pages, skips entirely when disabled, and stamps last_run_at on completed runs.

key_features.name: Onyx behavioral parity
key_features.description: The ported Onyx test suite (test_memory_recall_and_graph.py, the suite behind the Onyx testsprite brain-graph script) passes against the Rust crate with the same seed data, topology, and assertions.

validation_criteria: cargo build -p xai-grok-brain compiles with no errors and cargo clippy -p xai-grok-brain reports no warnings.
The crate's full cargo test suite (unit + consumer + onyx_parity integration tests) passes deterministically on repeated runs.
Graph invariants hold: duplicate edges collapse, self-edges error, degree-0 nodes appear in the graph query output.
Drifted source refs [s1], S1, [D3], d4 all resolve to their canonical S#/D# keys.
A disabled store never invokes the extraction provider and never stamps last_run_at; an enabled run stamps it even when no pages are produced.

test_environment.notes: Library crate; all validation runs through cargo from the workspace root. No live server.
